h1:
Surat Thani Cafes
In Town · On the Tapi River
intro: Surat Thani is more than just a stopover on the way to Koh Samui. The city has a cafe scene that keeps growing, from specialty coffee roasters in the old town near Talat Lang market to riverside spots on the Tapi River where you can sip coffee and watch the boats go by all day. We picked 10 cafes locals actually go to, and made it clear which ones win on coffee and which ones win on the riverside view.

blocks.html: If you're passing through Surat Thani while waiting for the ferry to the islands, or coming into town on its own, a cafe is the best place to escape the heat. The city's cafes fall into two clear camps: the coffee crowd, serious about beans and extraction, usually clustered in the town near the markets, and the atmosphere crowd, focused on Tapi River views and easy seating. We've ranked them by how each one stands out, and we'll tell you straight who each spot suits.

blocks.text: Ranking the 10 Best Cafes in Surat Thani

items.name: A3 Cafe & Specialty Coffee
items.blurb: A two-storey specialty cafe in the middle of town, on the corner across from the Hokkien shrine. White-toned decor with a little art gallery corner, and several single-origin beans to choose from. Serious coffee people in Surat usually mention this place first.
items.meta: In town, near Talat Lang · Soi Amphoe 3

items.name: Renovate • Espresso Bar
items.blurb: A tucked-away spot down a soi with plenty of room and easy seating — lots of tables and a warm feel. Creative drinks across both coffee and tea, plus a rotating seasonal menu. Good for settling in for a long stay.
items.meta: Makham Tia subdistrict, Soi Si Kasem (deep in Talat Mai)

items.name: Sipster Roaster
items.blurb: A loft-style cafe that roasts its own beans and serves as a meetup spot for the city's coffee crowd. The owner recommends the Dark Knight blend, and the cakes are house-made too. When it's busy you may wait a bit for your coffee and cake.

items.name: Common Activity & Art Space
items.blurb: A black-and-white riverside cafe on the Tapi with plenty of photo corners, a varied coffee menu, and easy parking. It opens early, so it's a good spot to catch the river breeze before midday.
items.meta: Talat Lang, Bang Kung, Mueang district · on the Tapi

items.name: Backyard Cafe x TCTC
items.blurb: A cafe right on the Tapi River with a backyard-garden feel. The cakes are made in-house from local community fruit and whatever's in season, and there are healthy smoothies, tea, coffee, and the occasional workshop.
items.meta: On the Tapi River, Mueang district

items.name: Latitude Coffee (Slow Bar)
items.blurb: A slow bar that pulls coffee gently and carefully, with several beans on offer. Good for anyone who wants to talk flavor with the barista — quiet and easy to settle into.
items.meta: Behind Mueang Surat school · in town

items.name: MezzoX Drip Cafe
items.blurb: A minimal, pared-back drip cafe that's easy on the eyes and focuses mainly on pour-over. Good for anyone who likes a clean black coffee and seating that doesn't get crowded.

items.name: Bamboo Cafe Food & Coffee
items.blurb: A riverside spot across from Wang Tai Hotel. By day it's a fresh-coffee cafe; at night it turns into a chill hangout with cocktails and cold beer, open late until midnight. Good for watching the sunset over the Tapi.
items.meta: On the Tapi River, across from Wang Tai

items.name: Hellophunphin
items.blurb: A hidden cafe on the Tha Kham side with a Japanese homestay feel in the old town and Tapi River views. Decorated in several corners and moods — good for quietly catching up on work or meeting friends.
items.meta: Tha Kham area (old town, opposite bank)

items.name: Cocolino Beach Club
items.blurb: A cafe on the Tapi River just past the entrance to Koh Lamphu, with a beach-club feel. Sip coffee by day and cold drinks in the evening, with a riverside vibe and prices that won't break the bank — good for lingering until dusk.
items.meta: On the Tapi, near the Koh Lamphu entrance

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Most specialty cafes in town close around 17:30–18:00, so if you want good coffee, go from morning to early afternoon. Many of the riverside cafes on the Tapi stay open into the evening — save those for sitting out at dusk and watching the sunset.

blocks.text: Pick a Cafe by Your Style

items.name: Serious coffee crowd
items.blurb: Want freshly roasted single origin? Go for A3, Renovate, Sipster Roaster, or Latitude, where the baristas can actually talk flavor with you.

items.name: Riverside view crowd
items.blurb: Want to sit and watch the Tapi River? Go for Common, Backyard, Bamboo, or Cocolino — more about atmosphere than the coffee.

items.name: Photo crowd
items.blurb: Want pretty corners for social? Common Activity's black-and-white look and Hellophunphin's Japanese old-town style give you plenty of angles.

blocks.text: Know This Before Cafe-Hopping in Surat

items: Main cafe areas — clustered in town near Talat Lang/Talat Mai and along the Tapi River, all just a few minutes apart by car or motorbike.
Prices — regular coffee starts around ฿50–80, while single-origin specialty drinks at some shops climb to ฿120–140 a cup.
Opening hours — in-town coffee shops focus on daytime and close in the evening, while many riverside spots stay open late into the night. Check the shop's page first, since some close on weekdays.
Parking — riverside spots like Common have easy parking, but cafes down the old-town sois have limited space. Go in the morning and it's easier to find a spot.

faq.q: Which Surat Thani cafes stand out for specialty coffee?
faq.a: If you're after serious coffee, go for A3 Cafe & Specialty Coffee, which has several single-origin beans, Renovate Espresso Bar, Sipster Roaster, which roasts its own beans, and Latitude Coffee, a slow bar. All of them are in town.

faq.q: Which riverside cafes on the Tapi River in Surat are worth recommending?
faq.a: Common Activity & Art Space with its black-and-white look and plenty of photo corners, Backyard Cafe x TCTC with a backyard-garden feel by the river, Bamboo Cafe across from Wang Tai that stays open until midnight, and Cocolino Beach Club near the Koh Lamphu entrance.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost at Surat Thani cafes?
faq.a: Regular coffee starts around 50–80 THB a cup, while single-origin specialty drinks at shops like A3 can climb to 120–140 THB, depending on which bean you choose.

faq.q: How late do cafes in Surat town stay open?
faq.a: Most specialty cafes in town open from morning until evening, roughly 08:00–18:00, with many closing around 17:30. Some riverside cafes on the Tapi River stay open into the evening or until midnight, such as Bamboo and Cocolino.

faq.q: Can I fit in a cafe in town while waiting for the ferry to Koh Samui?
faq.a: Yes, if you have the time, since most cafes are in town and along the Tapi River close together, just a few minutes apart by car. Just allow about an hour to travel from the city to the Don Sak ferry pier.
